title: Aim every task at the lesson question
statement: Give every task's writer the lesson's one question, and point each task that can serve it at what bears on it, preferring the lines a judge found help answer it.
detail: The lesson engine puts the lesson question into every block's prompt, and before any block is written it asks the judge, line by line, whether each line helps a careful reader answer that question (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/util.js`; `g9/transformer/src/analyse.js`). The evidence hunt's claim, the open check's key moment and the word web's big idea are each asked for because they bear on the question, and the quick check, open check and evidence hunt are also told up to eight of the lines the judge found most relevant (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/evidence-hunt.js`, `open-check.js`, `word-web.js`).
against: The relevant lines are a preference, not a rule: "Prefer them, but use any line that fits the task." (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/util.js`, line 41). The glossary, key words and word in focus are chosen for reading the text, not for the question.
